**Ch 074 draft — screening**

- "But as the side-ladder was being rigged, the stranger waved his hand in token that this was unnecessary." — In the source, "the stranger in question" (Captain Mayhew) waves his hand. In the draft, "the stranger" was introduced as "she was the Jeroboam of Nantucket. She ranged abeam… and lowered a boat." The boat's occupant hasn't been individually identified yet; "the stranger" here refers ambiguously to someone in the boat, but readers can infer it is the captain. Marginal but parseable by context. Not a gate-test failure.

- "So soon as this figure was descried, Stubb exclaimed—'That's he! that's he!—the long-togged scaramouch the Town-Ho's company told us of!'" — In the source, this is immediately followed by: "Stubb here alluded to a strange story told of the Jeroboam, and a certain man among her crew, some time previous when the Pequod spoke the Town-Ho. According to this account and what was subsequently learned, it seemed that the scaramouch in question had gained a wonderful ascendency over almost everybody in the Jeroboam. His story was this:" — The draft cuts all of that bridging explanation and jumps directly to "His story was this." The pronoun "His" now has no clear antecedent in the draft: "this figure" (the freckled man) is the only candidate, but Stubb's exclamation refers to "the scaramouch" as someone previously learned about from the Town-Ho, and the draft provides no sentence establishing who "His" refers to in the transition to the backstory. Let me check: draft reads "So soon as this figure was descried, Stubb exclaimed—[quote]" then next paragraph "His story was this." "His" = the figure's / the scaramouch's. The figure was described in the previous paragraph. A competent reader will connect "His story was this" to the just-described freckled man Stubb identified as the scaramouch. This is tight but traceable. Gate test: probably not genuinely confusing.

- "he left for Nantucket and shipped as green-hand on the Jeroboam." — Source says "he had left Neskyeuna for Nantucket." The draft just says "he left for Nantucket." Antecedent of "he" is the man in the backstory being narrated. Fine.

- "the archangel opened all his seals and vials, devoting the ship to unconditional perdition; the crew threatened in a body to leave if he were sent off, and Gabriel had the complete freedom of the ship." — "Gabriel" is introduced here as a name; in the draft the man announced himself as "the archangel Gabriel" earlier in this same paragraph. Name is established locally. Fine.

- "As the seamen resumed their work upon the jacket of the whale, many strange things were hinted in reference to this wild affair." — Source: "As, after this interlude, the seamen resumed their work upon the jacket of the whale…" The draft drops "after this interlude" but the sentence still parses. The "jacket of the whale" — is there a whale established in this draft chapter? Scanning the draft: the chapter involves the Jeroboam encounter; the hoisted sperm whale's head is mentioned in the source ("the hoisted sperm whale's head jogged about very violently") but that detail was cut from the draft. So "the jacket of the whale" references a whale being worked on shipside that was never established in the draft. Let me verify: the source has "the hoisted sperm whale's head jogged about very violently, and Gabriel was seen eyeing it with rather more apprehensiveness than his archangel nature seemed to warrant" — this was cut from the draft. And at the very end, source has "the seamen resumed their work upon the jacket of the whale" — retained in draft. The whale being processed alongside is a definite reference ("the jacket of the whale") that was established in the source passage that was cut. This is a mid-scene/dangling definite reference. A reader of the draft has no idea what whale is being worked on; no whale has been mentioned as alongside the ship in this chapter's draft. Gate test: a competent reader with no source access would be genuinely puzzled by "their work upon the jacket of the whale" — what whale? This is a real finding.

**Finding: Ch 074, final sentence — "As the seamen resumed their work upon the jacket of the whale" — "the whale" is a definite reference to a sperm whale being processed alongside the Pequod during the Jeroboam encounter, established in source by "the hoisted sperm whale's head jogged about very violently" but that line was cut from the draft, leaving the definite article stranded.**

This qualifies as **mid_scene_jump** (definite reference to an object not established in the draft chapter, established in the source passage that was dropped).

Let me do one final check on Ch 062 to make sure I haven't missed anything, particularly the Flask/Starbuck exchange — Flask asks "What was it, Sir?" and Starbuck answers. Who is "Sir"? Starbuck was named in the source as making the exclamation. In the draft, Starbuck's exclamation names him: "Starbuck still gazing at the agitated waters where it had sunk, with a wild voice exclaimed—" Yes, Starbuck is named as the speaker immediately before Flask's question. Fine.
